# Sounds — provenance and licence

**Both files in this directory are generated by `scripts/build-rest-tones.mjs`.
There is no third-party audio in this app.** Nothing here was recorded,
sampled, downloaded or adapted from anybody else's work, so there is no licence
to comply with and no attribution owed.

Regenerate at any time with:

```
node scripts/build-rest-tones.mjs
```

The script is deterministic — it writes the same bytes every run — so the
checked-in files can always be verified against it.

| File | What it is | How it is made |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| `rest-over.wav` | Rest is over. A rising two-note chime, 0.495 s | Sine at 880 Hz (A5) for 0.16 s, 35 ms of silence, sine at 1318.51 Hz (E6) for 0.30 s, each with a 6 ms attack and an exponential decay |
| `countdown.wav` | One tick of the 3-2-1 cue, 0.090 s | Sine at 659.25 Hz (E5), quieter and shorter than the chime so three ticks are not mistaken for the end |

Both are mono 16-bit PCM at 44.1 kHz. Uncompressed, because there is no encoder
to license and no decoder latency, and a cue that has to land on the second is
worth 50 KB.

## Why this matters enough to write down

These ship inside white-label binaries sold to gyms under their own brand. An
audio file with no recorded provenance looks exactly like one with a licence
until somebody asks, and by then it is in every install. The exercise catalogue
already taught this lesson — see `scripts/check-attribution.mjs`, which exists
to keep RepDB's required credit on screen. The cheapest way to have no
attribution problem is to own the asset outright, which is what generating it
achieves.

**If you ever add a sound you did not generate**, record its source and licence
in this table, keep the licence text alongside it, and make
`src/ui/sounds.ts`'s catalogue name it — an entry in the library with a blank
provenance column is the failure this file is written to prevent.
